headline: Post-quantum negotiated-group enforcement and a sync-correctness hardening pass
summary: After each handshake to a HermitStash server the client now verifies the negotiated key-exchange group is a post-quantum hybrid and refuses a classical fallback, and a broad correctness pass closes data-integrity gaps in rename detection, resync, the local state database, certificate rotation, and cross-platform path handling.

items.title: TLS connections enforce a post-quantum negotiated group
items.body: After each handshake to a HermitStash server, the client reads the negotiated key-exchange group and refuses the connection if it fell back to a classical group instead of a post-quantum hybrid — closing a silent-downgrade gap where the offered list was post-quantum-preferred but the negotiated result was never checked. The auto-update download path, which talks to a non-post-quantum CDN, logs the fallback instead of failing. Set HERMITSTASH_ALLOW_CLASSICAL_TLS=1 to permit a classical negotiation deliberately.

items.title: The diagnostic bundle no longer leaks secrets in log content or config paths
items.body: Log files in the support bundle are re-redacted at bundle time — redaction previously ran only when a line was first written, so a token already on disk shipped in the clear. The configuration snapshot is reduced to an explicit allow-list of fields, so home-directory certificate paths and the sync-folder location no longer ship, and the certificate summary carries only the common names rather than the full distinguished name.

items.title: Renames on case-insensitive and Unicode-normalizing filesystems no longer duplicate or churn state
items.body: A file the server calls Foo.txt and a local foo.txt on Windows or macOS used to map to two separate database rows for one on-disk file, and macOS's Unicode form differences produced phantom add/remove cycles. Paths are now normalized and case-folded consistently, and a server-supplied path is screened for reserved Windows names before it is written to disk.

items.title: Rename detection no longer moves the wrong file on content collisions
items.body: A delete-plus-create of two unrelated files with identical content — common for empty files — could be mistaken for a rename and move the wrong file on the server. Detection now requires matching size and name locality and skips zero-byte files.

items.title: Resync drains in-flight work before wiping local state
items.body: A resync used to clear the local database while uploads, downloads, and buffered rename-deletes were still in flight, so an in-flight operation could write into the just-cleared database or a stale timer could delete a file the resync was about to re-fetch. Resync now quiesces all in-flight work first.

items.title: Local-state writes are transactional
items.body: A rename and the full-reset operation now each commit as a single transaction, so a crash mid-operation can no longer strand the sync cursor ahead of an empty file set — which silently broke all future catch-up — or lose a file from the database.

items.title: Certificate-authority rotation validates and can roll back
items.body: A server-pushed certificate-authority rotation now validates the new certificate, key, and CA chain before swapping, keeps a backup, and recovers on the next boot if the swap is interrupted, instead of risking an unusable client identity on a malformed trio or a mid-write crash.

items.title: The file watcher reconciles after a recovery
items.body: When the watcher restarts itself after an event-queue overflow, the client now re-scans the folder for changes missed during the gap instead of resuming blind, so a burst of local changes during the overflow is no longer lost.

items.title: Oversized downloads are refused up front
items.body: A download that would not fit in the available disk space is now refused before it starts, rather than filling the disk and retrying the same file forever.

items.title: Selective-sync patterns warn on unsupported shapes
items.body: An include or ignore pattern using a glob shape the matcher does not support — which would silently match nothing — now logs a warning at startup, so a mistyped pattern is loud instead of quietly failing to back up a file. A path-qualified directory pattern now correctly excludes its whole subtree.

items.title: The API-key reference is honored, and an unreachable keychain reports an actionable error
items.body: The apiKeyRef configuration field is now read rather than ignored, and when the OS keychain stored a key but is unreachable on a later read, the client reports how to recover instead of failing with an opaque authentication error.
